new_defects.affected_lines: engine/validator.py lines 515-538 (appointments loop and formal-role reconciliation)
new_defects.finding_type: new defect (adjacent to N-12 candidate_ref consumption)
new_defects.observed: stage_b_role_ready=true; blocking_error_count=0; all eight dimensions PASS; no E-APPOINTMENT-RECORD / E-CANDIDATE-UNKNOWN / E-UNAPPROVED-APPOINTMENT
new_defects.recommended_fix: In the appointments loop, add: if ap.candidate_ref != role_records.get(role,{}).get('candidate_ref'): fail('role_assignment_completeness','E-APPOINTMENT-CANDIDATE-MISMATCH',...) . Also reject any appointment whose (candidate_ref, role) is not the authoritative pair for that role.
reproduction: load valid_five_person.json into an in-memory deep copy
new_defects.root_cause: The appointments loop validates that ap.candidate_ref is a registry key, that ap.role is known and that the role is in a formal state, but never asserts ap.candidate_ref == role_records[ap.role].candidate_ref. The reconciliation at lines 534-538 only checks that the role record's own ref has an appointment; it does not reject extra appointments for other candidates under the same role.
new_defects.scope_note: The N-11 and N-12 checks as specified all reproduce secure. D-01 was found while inspecting all candidate_ref consumption sites required by the N-12 instructions; it is reported as a new defect rather than a failure of N-11/N-12.
new_defects.security_impact: A candidate with no acceptance, approval, formal-appointment or onboarding evidence can be recorded as appointed to a formally filled role and the state still passes. Undermines the guarantee that appointments are backed by role-bound acceptance evidence, and enables visually confusable identities (c-p1 vs C-P1) to appear as co-appointees without detection.
